subject: Cosmos-Lite elevated 5xx/timeouts — incident & mitigation updates
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@stellarapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Cosmos-Lite elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Hi Elena,

We wanted to let you know we are seeing an elevated rate of 5xx responses and streaming timeouts for requests served by the "cosmos-lite" model backing your /generate endpoint.

What we see so far:
- First anomalies began at ~2028-05-17T08:55:00Z and peaked between 08:58–09:05Z.
- Approx 9% of generation requests to cosmos-lite returned 5xx or stream interruptions in that window.
- Affected routes: /generate (batch size 1–4), customer traffic from your region (us-west).

Immediate actions taken by Redwood:
- Automatically shifted 35% of traffic to cosmos-stable-v1 as a warm fallback.
- Temporarily increased retries and extended request timeouts for affected routing policy.
- Ops captured traces and a service log excerpt for the window (attached).

Next steps:
- Engineering is investigating a candidate regression in KV cache handling; Olga is on the investigation (cc). We expect an update within 60–90 minutes.
- If you have specific request_ids or user-visible errors from the same window, please forward them and we will correlate.

Apologies for the disruption — we recognize this impacts your users and are prioritizing remediation.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Cosmos-Lite elevated 5xx/timeouts — initial notice

Karthik,

Thanks for the heads up. We started seeing errors in our production customers around 08:58Z — several end users reported generation failures in the UI and we saw a spike in 502/504 in our logs.

Example request id: 20280517-ELN-10932 (timestamps match the window you mentioned). We also recorded a user-visible timeout followed by an automatic fallback to a cached response (which caused a stale output).

This is high severity for us — can you confirm whether the fallback split will affect tokenization or model outputs? We observed some tokenization differences on the fallback responses.

Also: any ETA for a fix or a recommended mitigation on our side (retries, backoff)?

— Elena
Elena Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering, StellarApps
elena.ramos@stellarapps.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Cosmos-Lite elevated 5xx/timeouts — internal ops/rollforward proposal

Folks — forwarding the customer report. Key asks: confirm root cause, ETA for mitigation, and whether we can do a targeted rollback for affected pools.

Summary of current hypothesis (ops):
- Symptoms: elevated 5xx + streaming interruptions tied to certain sequence lengths and repeated prefix lookups.
- Candidate cause: a recent micro-optimization in the KV cache path combined with a quantized kernel that under certain cache eviction patterns leads to memory pressure and worker OOMs.

Proposed immediate mitigation:
1) Rollback the KV cache micro-optimization on the cosmos-lite variant for the us-west pool (targeted binary toggle).
2) Increase autoscale headroom for cosmos-stable-v1 and shift up to 60% of traffic while we confirm stability.
3) Apply conservative retry/backoff guidance to the customer's SDK (suggested: exponential backoff with max 3 retries; preserve idempotency where possible).
4) Collect a 1-hour trace set and validate no tokenization differences on fallback responses.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook.pdf contains the exact rollback commands and validation checklist.

Olga — can you confirm feasibility and estimated time for the rollback? Marissa — I may need a quick approval to increase fallback traffic and a potential credit if the outage continues beyond 2 hours.

Karthik
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@stellarapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 17 May 2028 11:40:22 -0700
Subject: Cosmos-Lite incident update — mitigation complete, short-term RCA and next steps

Hi Elena,

Update and immediate remediation summary: we completed the targeted rollback of the KV cache micro-optimization for the cosmos-lite variant in your us-west pool at 11:02Z and increased fallback traffic to cosmos-stable-v1 while validation completed. Error rates returned to baseline by ~11:10Z.

Short-term root cause (interim):
- A recent runtime change intended to reduce memory churn in the KV cache produced an unanticipated eviction pattern when certain repeating prefix sequences are present. In combination with a quantized kernel, this caused transient memory pressure on a subset of inference workers and resulted in OOMs and 5xx responses for ~9% of requests during the peak window.

Actions taken:
- Rolled back the micro-optimization for the affected variant (11:02Z).
- Increased autoscale headroom and shifted up to 60% traffic to cosmos-stable-v1 while we validated outputs.
- Deployed a hotfix that tightens eviction thresholds and adds more conservative memory guards for quantized kernels (hotfix will be part of the formal release after testing).
- Collected full traces and aggregated logs — attached incident_report_summary.pdf and the original service_log_excerpt.txt.

Customer impact and compatibility notes:
- We validated tokenization and semantic parity between cosmos-stable-v1 fallback and cosmos-lite for sampled requests during the mitigation window; differences were limited to minor punctuation variation in ~0.6% of sample outputs.
- We recommend you adopt the conservative retry/backoff in your SDK for the next 48 hours (exponential backoff, max 3 retries) as an extra safeguard; this will reduce user-visible timeouts while we complete the postmortem.

Next steps and commitments:
- Detailed postmortem will be published to SUP-2319 by EOD tomorrow with full timeline and long-term remediation items (kernel validation harness, extended pre-release stress tests against repeating-prefix patterns).
- We're provisioning a goodwill credit for affected usage in this window (Marissa — will coordinate credit authorization).
- We'll schedule a 30-minute technical review with your engineering team to walk the postmortem and answer questions; proposed times: tomorrow 10:00–12:00 PT or 14:00–16:00 PT — please let us know what works.

Apologies again for the disruption. We're treating this as high priority and will share the final postmortem and an action tracker.

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
